To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the number of object pairs with nonempty intersection is about the same, up to a log factor, as the number of pairs with intersecting enclosing balls for sets of polyhedra with bounded aspect ratio and bounded scale factor, and that the number of enclosing balls that need to be tested for intersection is about the number of object intersections.

the number of enclosing balls that intersect is about the same, to within a factor of O(n), as the number of objects that intersect, for sets of objects of constant aspect ratio and constant scale factor.

(1) for sets of polyhedra with bounded aspect and scale factors, the bounding box method is asymptotically optimal; and (2) for sets of convex polyhedra, our algorithm is asymptotically faster than the previous algorithms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What is the asymptotic behavior of the ratio of enclosing ball-pairs to object-pairs in a family of polyhedra, when the polyhedra have bounded aspect and scale factors?
two questions: (i) What is the complexity of the collision detection problem for a set of polyhedra, with bounded aspect and scale factor?
the following questions: (i) What is the worst case behavior of the bounding box method for collision detection?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bounding box method, which is the simplest and most commonly used collision detection algorithm, is asymptotically optimal.
, in a set of polyhedra with bounded aspect ratio and bounded scale factor, the complexity of the collision detection problem is independent of the number of objects.
, for a family of convex polyhedra of bounded aspect and scale factors, the number of object-object collisions is the same as the corresponding number of enclosing ball collisions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bounding box method for collision detection is theoretically justified and practically useful.
we have developed a theoretical foundation for bounding box collision detection.
, if the objects have bounded aspect and scale factors, then the problem of collision detection can be solved in time proportional to the number of intersected objects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the worst case, the number of intersections of convex polyhedra in d dimensions with bounded aspect and scale factor is O(dn).
the bounding-box heuristic for detecting collisions in a set of polyhedral objects is theoretically justified.
the number of intersected pairs in a set S of polyhedra is independent of the size of the set.
